chunks: Fadala narrated from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is recommended that one perform tawaf three hundred and sixty circuits, corresponding to the number of days of the year; and if one is unable, then whatever tawaf one is capable of performing.

key_terms.أُسْبُوعاً: Circuits/rounds - singular of usbu' or dawran, referring to a single circuit of tawaf
key_terms.ثَلَاثَمِائَةٍ وَ سِتِّينَ: Three hundred and sixty - the specific number of circuits mentioned
key_terms.عَدَدَ أَيَّامِ السَّنَةِ: The number of days of the year - the symbolic reason for the 360 circuits
key_terms.فَمَا قَدَرْتَ عَلَيْهِ: Whatever you are capable of - the concession for partial performance
key_terms.يَطُوفَ: To perform tawaf - the ritual circumambulation around the Kaaba or other sacred sites
key_terms.يُسْتَحَبُّ: Recommended (mustahabb) - a legal ruling indicating a virtuous but non-obligatory act

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended number of tawaf circuits for expiation or general worship according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on expiation for a pilgrim’s inadvertent errors, this hadith establishes the voluntary performance of 360 circuits of tawaf to mirror the lunar year. It highlights the Shia emphasis on voluntary supererogatory acts as a means of spiritual refinement, while offering a pragmatic concession that the merit remains valid even if the full number is not completed due to physical or circumstantial limitations.
